summary: South Caicos Airport (XSC/MBSC) is the main gateway to South Caicos, one of the smaller inhabited islands in the Turks and Caicos archipelago. Located on the southern coast of the island, it primarily serves inter-island flights connecting to Providenciales and Grand Turk. The airport supports the island's growing eco-tourism and sport fishing industries while maintaining a relaxed, low-traffic atmosphere typical of the smaller TCI islands.
faqs:
Q: How do I get to South Caicos Airport?
A: The most common route is a short domestic flight from Providenciales International Airport (PLS), with several carriers offering regular service. Some flights also connect through Grand Turk.

Q: Are there international flights to South Caicos?
A: No, XSC handles only domestic flights within the Turks and Caicos Islands. International travelers must connect through Providenciales.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The terminal is small with basic amenities including a check-in counter and waiting area. It serves primarily as a quick turnaround point for inter-island travelers.

Q: Is the airport used for private charters?
A: Yes, private and chartered flights can be arranged, and the runway accommodates small to mid-size aircraft commonly used in regional Caribbean operations.
transport_tips: Most visitors arrange ground transfers through their hotel or rental agency in advance, as taxi availability is limited and the island is small enough to navigate easily. Rental cars and golf carts are popular options for exploring South Caicos at your own pace. Confirm pickup arrangements before landing, as the airport has no dedicated taxi stand.
local_tip: Pack light and bring reef-safe sunscreen in your carry-on—South Caicos is renowned for some of the best wall diving and bonefishing in the Caribbean, and you'll want to hit the water quickly after landing without waiting for checked luggage.
